communicate with / in / by

communicate withيتواصل مع شخص▸ I usually communicate with my teacher by email.
communicate inيتواصل بلغة معينة▸ He can communicate in English and French.
communicate byيتواصل عن طريق وسيلة▸ We communicate by phone every day.

memory, memorize & memorial

memoryذاكرة▸ He has a sharp memory.
memorizeيحفظ▸ He tried to memorize the new vocabulary.
memorialنصب تذكارى▸ The memorial was built to honor our soldiers.

mean, main, remain & remains

meanيعنى / يقصد / لئيم▸ I did not mean to hurt your feelings.
mainرئيسى / أساسى / الأهم▸ Traffic congestion is the main problem facing this area.
remainيظل / يبقى / يتبقى▸ Despite the changes, the basic rules remain the same.
remainsبقايا / رفات / أطلال▸ Little remains of the original historical structure.

📖 Reading & Listening

Reading Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters

0 / 0

Learning a foreign language opens the door to new cultures, ideas, and opportunities. If students learn a new language, they will be able to communicate with people from different countries, make international friends, and participate in global activities.

Moreover, they will understand other cultures better, which promotes respect, tolerance, and a broader worldview.

If students practiced speaking regularly, they would improve their confidence, fluency, and ability to express themselves clearly in different situations. Schools that provide language programs encourage students to use these skills in real-life experiences, such as traveling, participating in exchange programs, joining international competitions, or using digital communication tools to connect with peers worldwide.

Some students hesitate to learn another language because they feel it is too difficult or time-consuming. However, if they tried consistently and remained motivated, they would gain not only language skills, but also critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, memory improvement, and new perspectives on the world.

In addition, if students spoke multiple languages, they would have more opportunities for higher education and careers in international companies. In short, learning a foreign language is not just about grammar and vocabulary. It is a key to becoming a global citizen, expanding personal horizons, and contributing positively to a connected and multicultural world.

Listening My Journey as a Multilingual

0 / 0

"My name is Salma and I speak Arabic, English, and Spanish. I grew up in Cairo, but when I was 12, my family moved to Spain because of my father's job. At first, I couldn't understand anything at school. I felt shy, anxious, and overwhelmed. However, my teachers encouraged me to practice every day with my classmates, and slowly I improved. After a year, I could speak Spanish fluently and participate in class confidently.

Later, I returned to Egypt and studied English more seriously. Speaking three languages has completely changed my life. I am now multilingual, which allows me to work with international companies, travel easily, and communicate with people from different cultures. I believe learning languages is not just about words. It's about understanding people. We must respect the cultures connected to the languages we learn. In the future, I hope to study French. Who knows, maybe one day I will speak five languages."

📘 Language — Part 1 · Countable & Uncountable Nouns

Countable Nouns الأسماء المعدودة

الأسماء التى تُعد لها مفرد ويمكن أن يأتى قبلها واحدة من:
a – an – one – this – that – each – every …
ويأتى بعدها فعل مفرد: is – was – has – v + s
a bagthis careach boyone story
a bookthis tableeach studentone pen
an applethat busevery heroone cup
an eggthat watchevery boxone flat
الأسماء التى تُعد لها جمع بإضافة (s / es / ies) يمكن أن يأتى قبلها:
these – those – many – few – a lot of – several – some – any …
ويأتى بعدها فعل جمع: are – were – have – base infinitive
bagsthese carsmany boysfour stories
booksthese tablesfew studentstwo pens
applesthose busesany heroesa lot of cups
eggsthose watchessome boxeslots of flats

Uncountable Nouns الأسماء غير المعدودة

الأسماء التى لا تُعد أسماء ليس لها جمع ولا يأتى قبلها: a – an – one – these – those
ويأتى بعدها فعل مفرد: is – was – has  /  v + s
important uncountable nouns أسماء مهمة لا تُعد
information معلوماتmusic موسيقىtraffic مرور
news أخبارequipment المعداتelectricity كهرباء
furniture أثاثcloth قماشjewellery مجوهرات
advice نصيحةbaggage / luggage أمتعةrubbish قمامة
money مالtravel السفرwork عمل
bread خبزclothing الملبسhair شعر
time وقتmachinery آلات
ويمكننا تقسيم الأسماء التى لا تُعد كما يلى:
1. Liquids السوائلmilk – water – juice – tea – coffee – oil … etc.
2. Materials الخاماتgold – wood – paper – iron – glass – stone … etc.
3. Gases الغازاتoxygen – hydrogen – carbon dioxide … etc.
4. School subjects المواد الدراسيةhistory – physics – chemistry … etc.
5. Meals الوجباتbreakfast – lunch – dinner – supper
6. Languages اللغاتArabic – English – French – German … etc.
7. Sports الرياضاتtennis – football – volleyball – squash – hockey … etc.
8. Activities الأنشطةstudying – reading – writing – shopping … etc.
9. Abstract nouns الأسماء المجردةfreedom – advice – luck – honesty – love … etc.
10. Natural phenomena الظواهر الطبيعيةdrought – heat – snow – thunder – light – rain … etc.

Quantifiers محددات الكميات

a lot of – many – much – a few – few – a little – little
a lot of = lots of
تأتى قبل اسم يُعد جمع أو اسم لا يُعد، ويُفضل استخدامها فى الجملة الخبرية المثبتة.
  • I have got a lot of friends.
  • I have got lots of money.
many
تأتى قبل اسم يُعد جمع، ويُفضل استخدامها فى النفى والاستفهام.
  • I haven't got many friends.
  • Have you got many friends?
much
تأتى قبل اسم لا يُعد، ويُفضل استخدامها فى النفى والاستفهام.
  • I haven't got much money.
  • Have you got much money?
a few
تأتى قبل اسم يُعد جمع وتشير إلى عدد قليل ولكن يكفى (enough).
  • I have a few experiences.
few
تأتى قبل اسم يُعد جمع وتشير إلى عدد قليل ولا يكفى (not enough) — تنفى الجملة لذا لا تأتى فى الجملة المنفية.
  • I have few experiences.
a little
تأتى قبل اسم لا يُعد وتشير إلى كمية قليلة ولكن تكفى (enough).
  • I have a little money.
little
تأتى قبل اسم لا يُعد وتشير إلى كمية قليلة ولا تكفى (not enough) — تنفى الجملة لذا لا تأتى فى الجملة المنفية.
  • I have little money.
لاحظ: يُفضل استخدام (many – much) فى النفى والاستفهام، ولكن يمكن استخدامهم فى الجملة المثبتة إذا جاء قبلها (so – too – as) أو إذا أتوا قبل الفاعل:
  • He has so much money.
  • I have faced too many problems recently.

some & any

some
تأتى قبل اسم يُعد جمع أو اسم لا يُعد فى جملة خبرية مثبتة وفى سؤالَى العرض والطلب.
  • I found some good stories. (اسم يُعد)
  • I drank some water. (اسم لا يُعد)
  • Would you like some tea? (عرض)
  • Can I have some of these oranges? (طلب)
any
تأتى قبل اسم يُعد (مفرد أو جمع) أو اسم لا يُعد فى جملة استفهامية أو منفية أو فى الجملة الشرطية.
  • I don't want any problems. (اسم يُعد)
  • I didn't drink any juice. (اسم لا يُعد)
  • Do you have any experience? (سؤال)
  • If you find anything, contact me at once. (الجملة الشرطية)
وتأتى مع الكلمات الدالة على النفى مثل:
hardly – scarcely – seldom – never – without – refuse – too … to
  • He never had any luck. = He had no luck.
  • We hardly had any money.

Important Notes أسماء تُعد أو لا تُعد حسب المعنى

① بعض الأسماء يمكن أن تُعد أو لا تُعد حسب المعنى مثل:
الاسمالمعنىتُعد؟مثال

an ironمكواةتُعدShe bought an iron yesterday.
ironالحديدلا تُعدThis table is made of iron.
a chickenدجاجةتُعدI'd like to buy a chicken.
chickenلحم الدجاجلا تُعدDo you like chicken?
a companyشركةتُعدThe law obliges companies to pay decent wages.
companyصحبةلا تُعدYou should be in good company.
a time / timesمرة / مراتتُعدHe went to London three times.
timeالوقتلا تُعدDon't hurry. There's plenty of time.
a schoolمدرسةتُعدThe government built a school in our village.
schoolدراسةلا تُعدMy brother started school at the age of 6.
a coffeeفنجان من القهوةتُعدCould I have two coffees? (cups of coffee)
coffeeقهوة (مشروب)لا تُعدHave you got any coffee?

a lightمصباح كهربىتُعدWe need two lights in this room.

a glassكوب زجاجىتُعدWould you like a glass of water?
glassزجاجلا تُعدThe window's made of unbreakable glass.
a woodغابةتُعدWe went for a walk in the woods after lunch.
woodخشبلا تُعدThe house was built of wood but faced with brick.
a workعمل فنى / عمل أدبىتُعدWe need to build a new work in this area.
workالعمللا تُعدI've got so much work to do.

Kinds of Partitives أنواع أدوات التجزئة

② يمكن تحويل الأسماء التى لا تُعد إلى أسماء تُعد كالآتى:
1. General Partitives ألفاظ التجزئة العامة
باستخدام (a bit of – a piece of) كألفاظ تجزئة عامة، وفى الجمع (bits of – pieces of):
  • I'd like a piece (a bit) of cloth / bread / advice.
  • I'd like two pieces (bits) of cloth / bread / advice.
2. Special Partitives ألفاظ التجزئة الخاصة
a cup of فنجان منa bag of كيس منa sheet of فرخ من
a glass of كوب منa tin of علبة منa tube of أنبوبة من
a bottle of زجاجة منa slice of شريحة منa dish of طبق من
a jar of برطمان منa kilo of كيلو منa bar of قطعة من
a packet of علبة منa loaf of رغيف منa pair of زوج من
وعند الجمع نجمع لفظ التجزئة ولا نجمع اسم المادة:
  • two sheets of paper – two jars of jam – five cups of tea – two loaves of bread – two slices of meat – six bars of chocolate …

ملاحظات على الفعل مفرد أم جمع؟

③ العبارات الدالة على الكمية والمبالغ المالية والزمن والثمن والمسافة والوزن ودرجات الحرارة تُعامل معاملة المفرد مع الفعل:
  • Ten million pounds is a lot of money.
  • Fifty litres of petrol fills my car.
  • Five kilometers is a long way to walk.
  • Two hours is a long time to wait.
④ لاحظ الفعل مع:
a number of + فعل جمع  /  the number of + فعل مفرد
  • The number of people in Egypt is in increase.
  • A number of boys have left their books.
⑤ لاحظ الفعل مع:
One of the + اسم جمع + فعل مفرد
  • One of the players was injured.
  • One of the spokes of my bicycle was broken.
⑥ لاحظ مع هذه التعبيرات الفعل يتبع الفاعل الأول:
as well as / besides / in addition to / along with
  • I as well as he study hard.
  • He as well as I studies hard.
⑦ لاحظ مع هذه التعبيرات الفعل يتبع الفاعل الثانى:
not only … but also … / … or … / either … or … / neither … nor …
  • Neither Toka nor the students are here. (Neither the students nor Toka is here.)

📖 Reading & Listening — Part 2

Reading Ramy's Journey with English

0 / 0

Ramy had always dreamed of traveling abroad. One summer, he finally flew to Liverpool, England. At first, he was excited, but soon he felt anxious. His biggest difficulty was that he couldn't speak English. At the airport, he struggled to understand the officer's questions. He only smiled and showed his passport, hoping for the best.

In the city, life became more complicated. When he tried to buy a bus ticket, he couldn't explain himself. People behind him grew impatient, and he felt embarrassed. Later, at a restaurant, he wanted chickens but accidentally received fish.

That night, Ramy decided something important: he must learn English. He downloaded a language app, practiced basic phrases, and wrote down useful words. The next day, he tried saying, "One ticket, please," and "Chicken, please." To his surprise, people understood him! He felt more confident.

As days passed, Ramy spoke more words, greeted locals, and even asked for directions. People appreciated his efforts and were kind to him. By the end of his trip, Ramy realized that learning English had turned his journey from a struggle into an enriching adventure.

Listening Modern Technology and Learning Foreign Languages

0 / 0

Learning any foreign language has become easier thanks to modern technology.

In the past, students relied only on textbooks and classroom lessons. Today, digital tools provide many opportunities to practice and improve skills in fun and interactive ways. One of the most popular methods is using language learning applications.

These apps offer short daily lessons, vocabulary games, and much pronunciation practice. Many of them use artificial intelligence to adjust the level of difficulty according to the learner's progress. Some learners spend a little time every day, but they still make great progress. Another useful tool is online video and audio platforms. By watching movies, listening to songs, or following podcasts in the target language, learners can hear natural pronunciation and improve listening skills. Subtitles and playback options make it simple to understand and repeat. However, only a few students make full use of these options. Social media and messaging platforms also play a role.

Learners can connect with native speakers around the world, exchange messages, and even join live video calls. This creates real communication opportunities without traveling abroad, but some students show little interest in using these chances effectively.

Informal Email البريد الإلكترونى غير الرسمى

informal emailإيميل ودّى يُرسل لأشخاص غير رسميين (صديق / قريب) بأسلوب بسيط ومباشر
audienceالمُرسل إليه يكون شخصًا تعرفه: أصدقاء، أقارب، زملاء مقرّبون
purposeالدردشة، مشاركة أخبار، دعوة، تهنئة، سؤال سريع، ترتيب موعد
chatting, inviting a friend, sharing news
toneنبرة ودّية، بسيطة، طبيعية؛ جمل قصيرة، عدم التكلّف — a relaxed, friendly tone
subject (tips)Weekend plans? / Guess what! / Quick catch-up قصير وجذّاب
subject (avoid)تجنّب الصيغ الرسمية جدًا مثل Regarding… أو العناوين الطويلة
greeting (examples)Hi Sara, / Hello John, / Hey Ali, / Hi [First Name],
opening lineHow are you? / Hope you're doing well! / I just wanted to…
language (contractions)I'm, I'll, can't, don't, it's يُستحسن استخدام الاختصارات
language (vocabulary)كلمات يومية وبسيطة؛ تجنّب المصطلحات الرسمية أو التقنية المعقّدة
لا تستخدم Dear Sir/Madam, أو لغة رسمية جدًا، ولا تُطِل بلا داعٍ
emojisيمكن استخدامها باعتدال للتعبير الودّى
structure (overview)تحية → افتتاحية قصيرة → الغرض والتفاصيل → جملة ختام → توقيع
paragraphingفقرة قصيرة لكل فكرة؛ سطور مختصرة لتسهيل القراءة
sharing news (phrases)I've got great news… / Guess what happened…
inviting (phrases)Do you want to…? / Would you like to join us…? / Let's meet
asking a favorCould you help me with…? / Can you send me…?
arranging timeAre you free on…? / How about Saturday at 5?
softeners (ودية)maybe, a bit, just, I think, I'm not sure but… لتلطيف الطلب
closing linesTalk to you soon! / Can't wait to hear from you. / Thanks a lot!
sign-offsBest wishes, / See you soon, / Take care, / Love,

✍️Model answer نموذج إجابة
Social media
Social media has become an important part of our daily life. It helps us communicate with friends and relatives all over the world, share news and photos, and learn new things quickly. Students can use it to exchange notes and practice foreign languages with native speakers. However, social media also has some dangers. Spending too much time online wastes time, affects our health and can spread rumors and fake news. In short, social media is a useful tool if we use it wisely and in moderation.

B. Reading Comprehension العبور ٢٠٣٦ · 7 Q

0 / 0

Learners of foreign languages are divided into three categories or types. Some learners are not aware of the correct structure of sentence. They do not care about the parts of speech that constitute the sentence. They do not know what a noun, an adjective, an adverb, a verb, a pronoun, or a preposition is. Moreover, they do not know how to use them or where to use them in a sentence. For example, if you ask a student what part of speech "early" is in the following: "He has an early start" They may mistake a noun for a verb, an adjective for an adverb, or a pronoun for a preposition.

While some learners focus on memorizing vocabulary. They study them by heart, but they cannot use them in a context. Those learners do not pay attention to the derivatives that help them memorize new vocabulary easily and quickly.

Using vocabulary in context and memorizing them with derivatives makes them last for a long time. The last category or type is the learners who learn a foreign language as a subject, not a language. They find great difficulty in learning it.

1The best title for this passage is "………".
2What part of speech is "early" in "He has an early start"?
3To summarize how to learn vocabulary, ……… .
4There are ……… sorts of learners in the passage.
5The underlined word "They" refers to ……… .
6Dealing with a foreign language as a/an ……… is the best way to learn it.
7It's a disadvantage for a learner not to know the correct ……… of a sentence.
